Problem Statement 44 45 ### 1.1 Context 46 47 Zimmermann's storefront runs on SFCC B2C Commerce with a PWA Kit front end hosted on Managed Runtime (MRT). Editorial and CMS content (banners, homepage modules, navigation, footer, size guides, editorial blocks) is owned by Contentful and managed by the Zimmermann content team; commerce data (products, pricing, inventory, orders) is owned by SFCC. A dedicated Contentful squad will own the full Contentful setup under a separate statement of work; the Accenture squad must build and document the SFCC-side integration before that squad onboards. 48 49 ### 1.2 Problem 50 51 Editorial content authored in Contentful must render on the correct SFCC storefront pages. Some content is global; some must appear only on a specific category or product page. Contentful holds no knowledge of the SFCC catalogue, and the two systems must remain decoupled. The team needs one defined, correct mechanism for the PWA/MRT layer to decide which Contentful entries render on which SFCC page, cache-safely and consistently across the storefronts, together with a clear account of what the Accenture squad must build on the SFCC side (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration, integration wiring) before the Contentful squad onboards. 52 53 ### 1.3 Impact if Not Solved 54 55 Without a defined pattern the squad risks building inconsistent per-component ID-matching logic, coupling Contentful to the SFCC catalogue, or serving cached editorial content on the wrong category or product pages. The incoming Contentful squad would lack a briefing artefact, and integration blockers (credentials, per-environment configuration, unresolved content ownership) would surface late in the build. 56 57 ### 1.4 Success Criteria 58 59 1. One documented mechanism exists for scoping and rendering Contentful editorial content on the correct SFCC pages, decoupled from the SFCC catalogue. 60 2. The SFCC-side build scope (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration) is enumerated and traceable to Jira stories. 61 3. The Accenture versus incoming-Contentful-squad handoff boundary is defined. 62 4. Blockers and dependencies for the Contentful squad's onboarding are identified with owners. 63 5. The design is cross-checked against the codebase, Jira, and Confluence for accuracy. 64 65 *These criteria map to the validation in Section 6.* 66 67 --- 68 69 ## 2. Constraints & Assumptions 70 71 ### 2.1 Constraints 72 73 | Constraint | Detail | 74 | --- | --- | 75 | Platform | SFCC B2C Commerce + PWA Kit on MRT. No alternative platform is in scope. | 76 | Sole CMS | Contentful is the sole CMS across all storefronts (HPC-001). SFCC does not connect to Contentful directly; all CMS content is fetched by the MRT Node layer, not by SFCC cartridges or Business Manager. | 77 | Contentful environments | A single Contentful Space with one Environment per delivery tier (dev, test, sit, staging, uat, production), promoted sequentially. Production uses an alias for zero-downtime releases. Decided by Tim Lavelle (see Section 8). | 78 | Schema as code | Content types are Git-managed definitions deployed via CI (`npm run sync:contentful`), not hand-created in the Contentful UI. | 79 | Storefront and locale scope | The solution must work across 8 storefronts and 9 Contentful locales (serving 11 storefront-locale URL routes). US-domestic and US-international are two storefronts that share one SFCC site, in the same way EU-domestic's language variants share one SFCC site, so the 8 storefronts resolve to 7 SFCC Business Manager sites. No single-market workarounds. See Section 5.5. | 80 | Product data path | Product data reaches SFCC via AP21 through MuleSoft; Contentful editorial is independent of that path and never flows back to SFCC. | 81 82 ### 2.2 Assumptions 83 84 | Assumption | Risk if Wrong | 85 | --- | --- | 86 | Editorial content is fetched browser-direct (client-side) today; SSR-first fetching is the target architecture and is not yet built. | If SSR-first is not adopted, SEO/LCP-critical editorial renders client-side (spinner on first paint) and the SSR cache-key rules in Section 5 do not apply. | 87 | The Contentful "Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app" is installed and lets authors associate SFCC product/category references. | If the connector app's field type and payload shape differ from the assumed ShortText model, the content-model field definitions need revision (owned by SFCC-238). | 88 | US-International (REG-005) is a Confirmed requirement: a US-international checkout path (Global-e) alongside US-domestic, on the shared US SFCC site, reusing the `en-US` locale. | Its representation is not fully consistent across the SFCC site/routing configuration; confirm with the regional-config owner. Because it reuses `en-US`, the 9 Contentful locales are unaffected. Tracked in Section 7. | 89 | Sprint-2 content-type field sets are inferred from UI and Jira, not confirmed schema. | If the authoring review (Emma and Dani) changes them, the Sprint-2 definitions must be updated before build. | 90 | The Contentful account is on the Enterprise plan. | If not, the production alias (zero-downtime releases) is unavailable. | 91 92 --- 93 94 ## 3. Options Analysis 95 96 > The core design question this spike was tasked to answer is how Contentful editorial content is scoped to, and rendered on, the correct SFCC pages. Only one genuine options decision exists here. The other architectural choices are settled elsewhere (single Space versus multiple Spaces was decided by Tim Lavelle and is recorded in Section 2 and Section 8) or are current-versus-target build-status gaps (client-side versus SSR-first fetch, covered in Section 5), not options to weigh in this document. 97 98 ### 3.1 Options Summary 99 100 | Option | Pros | Cons | Viable? | 101 | --- | --- | --- | --- | 102 | **A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering** | + Keeps Contentful and SFCC decoupled (no catalogue duplication or sync).
+ SSR-first: editorial content is in the initial HTML (SEO, no content flash).
+ Components stay presentation-only and reusable across ID scopes.
+ The ID is a structural, non-localized field: one value across all locales. | - Authors enter a raw ID with no referential-integrity check against the live catalogue (typo risk).
- SSR cache keys must include the SFCC ID or cached content leaks across pages.
- Filtering logic is centralised in the MRT SSR layer, which must be correct. | Yes (recommended) | 103 | **B - Mirror the SFCC catalogue into Contentful and use reference fields** | + Authors select real products/categories (referential integrity, no typos). | - Requires a sync pipeline from SFCC to Contentful (build, maintain, drift).
- Couples the two systems.
- Disproportionate to current editorial volume. | Considered, not selected | 104 | **C - Filter client-side in the React component** | + Simplest to implement initially. | - Editorial content absent from the SSR HTML (SEO loss, content flash).
- Ships unneeded entries to the browser.
- Puts matching logic in the component, breaking the presentation-only contract. | No | 105 ### 3.2 Option Detail 106 107 #### Option A - SFCC ID + MRT SSR-side filtering 108 109 SFCC product and category IDs are stored as plain, non-localized ShortText fields (`sfccProductId`, `sfccCategoryId`) on the Contentful content type. At render time the MRT SSR layer fetches all published entries of a content type for the current locale, filters them by matching the ID field against the current page context, and passes only the matched entries to a presentation-only React component. A null ID means "show on all pages of this type". This fits the decoupling and SSR/SEO constraints in Section 2 and is detailed in Section 5. 110 111 #### Option B - Mirror the catalogue into Contentful (not selected) 112 113 Editors would pick real SFCC products/categories via Contentful reference fields backed by a synchronised copy of the catalogue. This removes the typo risk but requires a sync pipeline and couples the two systems; it is disproportionate to the current editorial volume. 114 115 #### Option C - Client-side filtering *(Discarded)* 116 117 Discarded: fetching all entries and filtering in the browser keeps editorial content out of the SSR HTML, which violates the SSR-first / SEO constraint and pushes ID-matching logic into components. 118 119 --- 120 121 ## 4. Recommended Option & Rationale 122 123 ### 4.1 Recommended Option 124 125 **Option A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering.** 126 127 ### 4.2 Rationale 128 129 Option A is the only approach that keeps Contentful decoupled from the SFCC catalogue while placing editorial content in the server-rendered HTML (satisfying the SSR/SEO constraint) and keeping components presentation-only. Option B solves the authoring typo risk but pays for it with a sync pipeline and coupling not justified by the current editorial volume; Option C is disqualified by the SSR/SEO constraint. Reference-resolution (turning an ID into rendered commerce data) is out of scope for this document and is owned by SFCC-238. 130 131 ### 4.3 Trade-offs Accepted 132 133 - Authors enter SFCC IDs by hand with no referential-integrity guardrail (typo risk). The installed Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app may improve the authoring step; the field mechanic is confirmed by SFCC-238. 134 - Every SSR cache key for an ID-scoped page must include the SFCC ID; omitting it leaks editorial content across category or product pages. 135 - This is proposed design, not yet implemented. Adopting it also commits to the not-yet-built SSR-first fetch (Section 5). 136 137 --- 138 139 ## 5. Technical Implementation 140 141 ### 5.1 High-Level Sequence (target SSR-first flow) 142 143 1. A shopper requests an SFCC page (for example a PLP for category X). 144 2. The MRT SSR layer fetches all published Contentful entries of the relevant content type for the current locale via the Contentful Delivery API (CDA). 145 3. The SSR layer filters entries by matching the SFCC ID field (`sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId`) against the current page context; a null ID means show on all pages of that type. 146 4. The SSR layer passes only the matched, pre-filtered entries to the React component. 147 5. The component renders the entries it receives, in order. If the array is empty it renders nothing (null return, no DOM output). 148 6. The SSR response is cached with a key that includes locale + the SFCC ID (+ page number if paginated). 149 7. On editor publish, Contentful fires an HMAC-signed webhook to the MRT receiver, which purges the affected cache keys. 150 151 > **Current state:** steps 2 to 5 run client-side today (`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`, a `useEffect` REST fetch with `include=2` for linked assets). ----- marcelannavarro [CHANGES_REQUESTED] -----
## Review: Requesting Changes

I'm requesting changes on a few items before merge. One of them is a genuine architecture decision that's really yours to make, since you own both the code and the integration doc.

### Must Resolve Before Merge

**1. The Contentful preview (CPA) token is reaching the browser.**
In both `contentfulPreview/index.tsx` and `experience/index.tsx`, the client is built client-side with the preview token and points at `preview.contentful.com` directly. Since `config/default.js` (~L186–190) serializes `previewAccessToken` into the same bundle as the delivery token, on any environment where `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` is set the token ships to the browser — where it can be lifted and used to read every unpublished draft in the space.

This contradicts our confirmed integration doc `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` §3/§4/§9: *"CPA token held server-side in MRT; never reaches the browser; requests proxied through an MRT preview endpoint."*

Same root cause, related: in `experience/index.tsx`, `resolvedToken` prefers the preview token even when `isPreview` is false — so normal `/:slug` traffic hits the preview host and can serve drafts on any env with the token set.

Since you own both the code and that doc, the real question is intent:
- If client-side preview is a deliberate call (Studio licence, simpler) → let's update §3/§4/§9 to match, add a hard "non-prod only" gate on the token, and get it signed off.
- If not → route the draft fetch through an MRT proxy so the token stays server-side (the doc's design).

**2. The `/preview` route is ungated on production and not `noindex`.**
`routes.tsx` registers it unconditionally with SSR on, so it's live and crawlable on the customer site — SEO duplicate-content risk, and it's the missing safety net that would turn a stray prod preview-token into a public draft leak. Gate it to preview environments (e.g. 404 when there's no preview token) and add `noindex`. This mostly rides along with whichever option we pick for #1.

### Should-Fix
- `experience/index.tsx`: `useFetchBySlug` is called after the `if (!client) return`, which breaks the Rules of Hooks. The new preview page already shows the right pattern (fetch inside a child component) — mirror it here.
- `contentfulPreview/index.tsx`: drop the `console.log` — we don't have a project logger yet, so remove rather than replace.
- `contentfulPreview/index.tsx`: the `getEntry` effect can let a stale response overwrite a newer one — add a cancel guard and clear state on `entry`/`locale` change.
- Both pages duplicate the client-creation logic — worth extracting into one shared hook, which is also the single place the #1 fix should live.

### Non-Blocking / Unrelated
- `.mcp.json` adds `b2c-dx-mcp` pinned to `@latest` with `--allow-non-ga-tools`, project-wide. It's unrelated to preview — I'd split it into its own PR, and pin a version either way. (CodeRabbit flagged this one as Major.)

### CodeRabbit Cross-Check
I re-ran a full CodeRabbit review to verify, and it independently surfaced the same core findings — the client-side preview token, the `/:slug` draft-leak, the Rules-of-Hooks issue, the `console.log`, the race condition, and the `.mcp.json` pin — and it also landed on **Request changes**. So we're aligned on the diagnosis.

Two of its suggested fixes need a small adjustment for our repo:
- It suggests replacing the `console.log` with "the project logger" — we don't have one, so just remove it.
- Its quick `isPreview ? previewAccessToken : accessToken` diff only stops *normal* traffic leaking; it doesn't take the token out of the browser, so it's a partial fix, not the resolution for #1.

What it couldn't flag are the bits that make this "reconcile before merge" rather than optional: CodeRabbit doesn't read `.docs/`, so it raised the token issue on generic security grounds without tying it to our confirmed integration doc, and it doesn't see the SEO/`noindex` gap or the tier/ownership process. That's the layer this review is adding.

**Re: preview token client-side (contentfulPreview/index.tsx and experience/index.tsx)**

Both findings flag the Contentful Preview Access Token (CPA) being used in the browser. This is intentional by design for two distinct reasons:

1. **`/preview` route** — This route exists solely for Contentful editors to trigger Live Preview from inside the Contentful web app. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK requires the CPA in the browser to subscribe to real-time content updates over a postMessage channel. The route is not linked from any storefront navigation and is only reachable via the preview URL configured in Contentful settings — it's not a public-facing page.
